'''''Adiantum raddianum''''', the '''Delta maidenhair fern''', is one of the most popular [[fern]]s to grow indoors.<ref name = MBG>[http://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?kempercode=b573 Adiantum raddianum], Missouri Botanical Garden.</ref> It is native to [[South America]] and its common name comes from its shiny, dark leafstalks that resemble human hair.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Delta Maidenhair Fern - Adiantum Raddianum - Indoor Care And Description|url=https://www.houseplantsexpert.com/delta-maidenhair-fern.html|access-date=2021-03-31|website=www.houseplantsexpert.com}}</ref> It typically grows about {{convert|17-19|in|cm|abbr=on}} tall and up to {{convert|22|in|cm|abbr=on}} wide.<ref name=":2" /> In the wild, it is found on [[forest floor]]s, rock crevices, river banks, coastal cliffs, and basalt banks along trails and streams.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|date=November 20, 2019|title=Adiantum raddianum (delta maidenhair fern)|url=https://www.cabi.org/isc/datasheet/3237#tosummaryOfInvasiveness|url-status=live|access-date=March 31, 2021|website=CABI Invasive Species Compendium|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150302145021/http://www.cabi.org:80/isc/datasheet/3237 |archive-date=2015-03-02 }}</ref> The triangular [[frond]]s are semi-erect in the beginning then droop gracefully as they age and can be up to {{convert|12|in|cm}}<ref>[http://plants.ces.ncsu.edu/plants/all/adiantum-raddianum/ Adiantum raddianum], NC Cooperative Extension.</ref> long by {{convert|6|in|cm}} wide. The genus name ''Adiantum'' comes from the [[Greek language|Greek]] word "adiantos", meaning "unwetted" (in reference to the leaves).<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|date=2020-05-17|title=Maidenhair Fern: How To Grow and Care For Adiantum Raddianum|url=https://plantcaretoday.com/maidenhair-fern.html|access-date=2021-03-31|website=Plant Care Today|language=en-US}}</ref>

This plant is [[hardiness (plants)|hardy]] down to {{convert|5|C|F|abbr=on}}, so must be grown indoors in [[temperate climate|temperate]] regions. However it may be placed outside in a sheltered spot during the summer months.<ref name = RHSPF/> It requires high humidity, well-drained soil, bright indirect light, and a fairly constant temperature.<ref name = MBG/> It prefers neutral or slightly alkaline soil and is suitable for [[Hardiness zone|USDA hardiness zones]] 10 and 11.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Adiantum raddianum (Delta Maidenhair)|url=https://www.gardenia.net/plant/adiantum-raddianum-delta-maidenhair-fern|access-date=2021-03-31|website=Gardenia.net}}</ref> It can be susceptible to [[Scale insect|scale]] and [[mealybug]].<ref name=":0" /> The cultivars ‘Brilliantelse’ and ‘Kensington Gem’ have won the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref name = RHSPF>{{cite web
|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/20650/Adiantum-raddianum/Details
|title=''Adiantum raddianum''
|publisher=Royal Horticultural Society
|accessdate=3 January 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web 
| url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf
| title = AGM Plants - Ornamental
| publisher = RHS 
| date = 2017
| accessdate = 3 January 2018}}</ref>

''A. raddianum'' is sometimes considered [[Invasive species|invasive]] in [[Hawaii]] and [[French Polynesia]].<ref name=":1" />
